user.title: Storage Manager
user.description: Adds a sidebar panel that shows what uses your disk and lets you reclaim space safely. Nothing is deleted without your confirmation.

data.backup_before_delete: Back up before deleting from the database
data.targeted_backup: Targeted backup with undo instead of a full backup

data_description.low_space_percent: Create a repair issue when free space drops below this share.
data_description.forecast_warning_days: Days until the disk is full according to the growth trend.
data_description.backup_rotation: Delete local backup copies that fall outside the daily/weekly/monthly schedule when you run a cleanup.
data_description.require_offsite: Keep a local copy unless the same backup exists on another location (NAS, cloud).
data_description.backup_before_delete: Before history or statistics are deleted, a backup of Home Assistant with the database is created and verified. A backup with the database from the last six hours is reused.
data_description.targeted_backup: For orphaned history, statistics, dead entities and events, only the rows that are deleted are saved, and the history offers Undo. If that is not possible (too many rows, too little space), the full backup is created as before. The global purge always uses the full backup.
data_description.nightly_run: Applies the retention tiers and the long-term statistics limits every night. Turn it off to run the action storage_manager.run_nightly from your own automation instead.

heavy_writers.title: Entities suddenly write far more history
heavy_writers.description:
{count} entities write at least ten times as many rows per day as usual (usual → now): {entities}

This often follows an update of a device or an integration. Open Storage Manager → Database to see the entity, shorten its history or switch it off, or mark the new rate as normal there. Throttling at the source (for example in ESPHome) helps most.

database_damaged.title: The recorder database is damaged
database_damaged.description:
SQLite's integrity check found errors: {details}

Storage Manager deletes nothing from the database until a check passes again. When Home Assistant itself runs into the damage, it moves the database aside and starts a new, empty one. See the recorder documentation for your options, restore a backup if you need the old history, and run the check again from the Storage Manager panel.
